Goals.Goal: **Exclusive candidate acquisition and bounded cleanup.** `ngrace spec new` and the implicit mint inside `ngrace supersede` acquire their candidate directory atomically — a non-recursive leaf `mkdir` whose `EEXIST` refuses — so losing the existence-check-to-create race writes nothing rather than overwriting a competitor. A competitor's `spec.xml` and any foreign file are preserved. Cleanup removes a directory only when this invocation created it and holds no artifact this invocation did not write at the moment of removal; on any refused check it preserves the residue and emits exactly one diagnostic naming the directory. The supported boundary is exact: identity mismatch, changed own bytes, foreign entries, an ordinary removal I/O failure, and `rmdir` `ENOTEMPTY` are refused and preserved; a non-cooperating replacement of this invocation's own file between the byte comparison and the unlink is outside the supported model and is not claimed safe; SIGKILL/power loss is the separate uncatchable window.

**Candidate-lock cooperation and evidence boundaries.** Stale-lock reclamation is token/identity-checked under the ratified tripartite rule (a parseable known-live holder is never stolen for age; a parseable known-dead holder is reclaimed immediately; an empty/unparseable/unknown holder waits for `CANDIDATE_LOCK_TTL_MS`; a token-mismatched release is a no-op). `recordAttempt` acquires the candidate lock at the approved public entry and snapshots WriteEvidence under it. The WriteEvidence filter matches only the exact canonical engine path and never a user file that merely shares a basename. `writePlanNew` waits/revalidates for a live publisher and refuses crash marker residue before its first write. `regenerateCursor({apply:true})` acquires at public entry before resolving or reading.

**The supersede transaction validates before it writes and cleans up on every post-mint failure.** All successor existence/location and lineage validation, and predecessor status/archive/replacement validation, run before `discardAndFoldEpoch` and before every other write. A rollback failure cannot bypass successor cleanup: the post-mint owner attempts cleanup once on every failure, records the outcome always, and surfaces a residual-state diagnostic exactly once only when cleanup preserves residue, and never recurses. The persistent-rollback composition is binding: the original failure and the rollback residue are always composed, and the cleanup diagnostic is composed only when cleanup preserved residue.

**The review verdict carries the approved three-phase snapshot.** `recordReviewVerdict` snapshots bundle location, directory identity, and exact prerequisite `spec.xml`/ledger bytes, evaluates CloseEvidence outside the lock, then reacquires and compares all of them before rebuilding from fresh ledger state and writing. A stale location, identity, spec, or ledger refuses.

**The generated successor id is operational identity data.** The successor wrapper and path, the successor plan's assertions and commands, the scope guard identity and activation switch, the payer pins and their tests, and the registry row `name` carry the successor id. Explicit predecessor lineage and the exact predecessor archive path remain permitted history/governance data.

AcceptanceCriteria.AC-MINT-EXCLUSIVE: Two exclusive-acquisition directions are driven, for both `ngrace spec new` and the implicit mint in `ngrace supersede`. (a) With a competitor's `spec.xml` present in the resolved directory (planted after the existence check, before creation, by isolated-process interception that reports it fired), the command exits non-zero and the competitor's `spec.xml` is byte-identical afterward. (b) With the directory absent, the command exits 0 and the new `spec.xml` is created exclusively (an existing `spec.xml` is never truncated). Pre-existing candidates under `active/` and `archive/` refuse. Acquisition is not the whole contract: cleanup is asserted separately by `AC-CLEANUP-BOUNDED`. Controls run against an isolated baseline copy where the pre-repair overwrite must be observed.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-CLEANUP-BOUNDED: Exclusive acquisition and bounded cleanup are driven on disposable fixtures with the exact surviving bytes asserted, and the **actual primitives' behavior is demonstrated**: a non-recursive `mkdir` returns `EEXIST` on an existing leaf; a non-recursive `rmdir` returns `ENOTEMPTY` with a foreign entry present and does not remove it; `stat` identity distinguishes a same-path replacement. Interleavings: (a) losing the leaf `mkdir` race refuses and writes nothing; (b) a **same-path replacement** of the acquired directory (removed/recreated or renamed-away-and-recreated) is detected by identity and forces preserve-and-refuse with a diagnostic naming the directory; (c) a **same-path modification** of this invocation's own `spec.xml` is detected by the byte comparison and forces the same; (d) a differently named foreign sentinel present at removal forces preserve-and-refuse; (e) a **controlled cleanup I/O failure** (injected at the actual removal boundary) forces preserve-and-refuse and leaves the directory; (f) an invocation-created directory holding no foreign artifact is removed on a handled refusal, so the common refusal leaves no successor. Repetition: the cleaned fixture repeated with the same resolved id keeps the count unchanged; the retained-residue fixture repeated with the same id adds no directory; a new-timestamp retry is asserted to resolve a new id and is reported, not hidden. The uncatchable-interruption case is **not** simulated as a handled refusal and is **not** asserted to emit a diagnostic. The supported boundary is exact: (b), (c), (d), and (e) are the handled cases; a non-cooperating writer that replaces this invocation's own file **after** the byte comparison and **before** the `unlink` is outside the supported model — no portable primitive provides atomic delete-if-unmodified — and is not asserted safe; the uncatchable SIGKILL/power-loss window is likewise not claimed closed. A mock may not be claimed to close the race unless it intercepts the actual vulnerable boundary (`rmdir`/the byte check).
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-CLEANUP-VALIDATE-FIRST: A foreign marker token or other failed ownership check leaves `spec.xml`, the marker, and the directory byte-identical, with `removed=false`, because validation precedes the first delete.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-CLEANUP-LOCK-API: Exported `cleanupCandidate` acquires the documented reentrant candidate lock itself, so a caller cannot invoke it without the lock; nested calls reuse the reentrancy depth.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-CANDIDATE-RECLAIM-EXCLUSIVE: Reclaim scheduling is deterministic through a fired seam/barrier: contender **B** observes the stale token; contender **A** reclaims and acquires the replacement lock; then B, holding only its stale snapshot (it never acquired a token), attempts reclamation. Assert the callbacks never overlap, A's replacement token and lock bytes survive byte-for-byte **while A still holds the lock**, and B is pending or aborts without removing A's file. Mismatched-token release is a **separate control** using a stale former owner token: that release is a **no-op** and preserves the current holder's bytes. A third control proves that B, after A releases and B acquires its own lock, removes **only its own** lock on a matching-token release. A successor-lock preservation control proves the loser cannot unlink a holder it did not create. Driven on the real exported boundary with recursive byte snapshots.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-ATTEMPT-SNAPSHOT-UNDER-LOCK: On the real CLI, an attempt that waits for a live candidate publisher then succeeds records WriteEvidence that includes the file changed during the wait, proving the snapshot happens under the lock and not before it.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-EVIDENCE-FILTER-CANONICAL-ONLY: For a git-backed fixture, only the exact canonical engine path `.ngrace/changes/active/.candidate-<valid C-ID>.lock` is filtered from WriteEvidence. Near-miss files remain **visible**: the same basename under the archive (`.ngrace/changes/archive/...`), a nested active directory (`.ngrace/changes/active/sub/.candidate-X.lock`), a malformed candidate id (`.ngrace/changes/active/.candidate-not-a-change.lock`), `src/.candidate-REAL.lock`, and a `.candidate-X.lock` in another top-level directory. Each near miss is asserted present in WriteEvidence; only the canonical engine path is absent.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-PLAN-NEW-MARKER-REFUSAL: Two reachable rows, not one impossible premise. (a) **Live publisher (a real paused `spec new`):** drive a real `ngrace spec new` paused after the `spec.xml` write; observe `status=draft`, the in-bundle marker `<bundle>/.ngrace-mint-owner`, the held sibling candidate lock `active/.candidate-<C-ID>.lock`, and no `plan.xml`. While the publisher holds the lock, `plan new` must remain **pending and byte-invariant** (no `plan.xml`); after the publisher releases, the contender reacquires, revalidates, and refuses on the draft-spec prerequisite without writing `plan.xml`. Then approve that published spec through the normal verb and prove a retry creates the plan. (b) **Crash-residue discriminator:** plant an **approved** `spec.xml` beside a **stale marker with no live publisher**, so the ordinary approved-spec prerequisite cannot explain the refusal; `writePlanNew` must refuse **before** writing `plan.xml` or any ledger change, with a diagnostic naming the unpublished candidate/marker. No row requires an approved spec beside a live publisher, which cannot exist.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-REGEN-ENTRY-LOCK: `regenerateCursor({apply:true})` is driven with the **default** `allowDirty:false`: a dirty condition is created while a live publisher holds the candidate lock; the contender must remain **pending** and byte-invariant; after the publisher releases, the contender acquires, revalidates, and returns the post-lock **dirty refusal** without writing. A clean tree or an `allowDirty:true` control does not satisfy this criterion.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-REFUSE-PRESERVES-CANDIDATES: After a refused implicit supersede, a pre-existing directory at the id a fresh mint would target is byte-identical (recursive SHA-256), and an explicit `--replacement` target is never deleted or rewritten. Handled concurrent modification (identity/content differences visible at validation, foreign names visible at enumeration, `rmdir` `ENOTEMPTY`) is preserved with an honest refusal, not removed. A non-cooperating replacement of this invocation's own file between byte validation and unlink is outside the supported model and is not asserted safe.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-SUPERSEDE-VALIDATE-BEFORE-FOLD: Each of the following refuses **before** any `discarded` write, fold, or governance bytes, leaving the ledger byte-identical and every loose file present: (a) an existing implicit successor under `active/`; (b) an existing implicit successor under `archive/`; (c) a missing predecessor `spec.xml`; (d) an archive-destination conflict; (e) an invalid predecessor spec status (e.g. applied); (f) an invalid predecessor plan status; (g) malformed predecessor artifacts; (h) an invalid lineage relation. **Explicit `--replacement` rows, with the same pre-discard/pre-fold byte invariance and under-lock revalidation:** (i) a **missing replacement** (no directory under `active/` or `archive/`); (j) a replacement **relocation/existence race** — the replacement moves between `active/` and `archive/`, or appears/disappears, between the preflight check and the write — refused under the revalidated lock, with the revalidation firing. The invalid-lineage row (h) stays separate from the explicit replacement existence/location rows. Each is driven on a disposable project with recursive SHA-256 snapshots and a direct exit.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-SUPERSEDE-ROLLBACK-CLEANUP: The exact red sequence is driven: the spec status write **succeeds**, the plan status write **fails**, then the spec rollback write **fails persistently**. Failing the first status write is nondiscriminating and does not satisfy this criterion. Assert: exactly one successor cleanup attempted and its outcome recorded; the original plan-write failure and the persistent spec-rollback residue are always composed into the reported error, and the single bounded cleanup diagnostic is composed exactly once only if cleanup preserved residue (a successful cleanup composes no residual diagnostic); no recursion; the predecessor spec is left in its last-successfully-written state (the spec-write state) and that residue is named; no invocation-created successor remains active unless cleanup was itself refused, in which case the residual is named exactly once.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-REVIEW-VERDICT-THREE-PHASE: The three-phase snapshot is driven with four separate cases: (a) a **spec-byte** mutation between snapshot and write; (b) a **ledger-byte** mutation; (c) a **same-path directory replacement with byte-identical prerequisites** (identity-only change); and (d) an **active/archive relocation** (location-only change). Each must refuse with no verdict/ledger write beyond the CloseEvidence command's own mutation, and the command's post-mutation bytes are preserved. A clean, unchanged prerequisite writes successfully. The verdict is never written against a stale location, identity, spec, or ledger state.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-COOPERATING-WRITER-COVERAGE: The complete covered outer-writer population and its fixtures are enumerated. Mutation writers, each with both a crash-residue refusal fixture and a live-publisher wait fixture, driven against the candidate-lock cooperation boundary: `writeSpecNew`, `writePlanNew`, `stampApproveArtifact`, `regenerateCursor({apply:true})`, `advanceCursor`, `recordAttempt`, `recordVerificationUnavailable`, `foldEpoch`, `recoverCursor({fix:true})`, `appendCommandRunEvent`, `recordCalibrationRestatement`, `discardAndFoldEpoch`, `recordGateDecision`, `recordReviewVerdict`, and the outer transaction `supersedeChangeBundle` (it acquires the sorted candidate locks and asserts publication, so a marker-bearing candidate is refused or waited on and never mutated). `advanceCursor`'s exported aliases `pauseCursor` and `resumeCursor` are named as aliases that delegate to `advanceCursor` and share its outer candidate-lock boundary and fixtures. The exported creation wrappers `mintResolvedBundle` and `mintBundle` are mapped explicitly to the `writeSpecNew`/`publishSpecNew` creation-and-publication transaction and share its live/crash fixtures; they are not hidden behind "wrapper-only aliases". **`cleanupCandidate` is carved out of that universal fixture sentence:** it remains a covered exported self-locking destructive boundary (`AC-CLEANUP-LOCK-API`), but a live-publisher or crash-residue fixture is not reachable — the lifecycle returns an `AcquiredCandidate` only after publication and handles prepublication failures internally, and a crash returns no record, so requiring a live/crash fixture would force a fabricated object. Its reachable discriminators instead are: (i) nested cleanup during a handled mint failure, proving reentrant lock use and the validated delete order; (ii) standalone cleanup of a returned, published `AcquiredCandidate`, driven while another process holds that candidate lock, proving it waits, revalidates, and removes only bytes it still owns; and (iii) the foreign-token/content/identity/`ENOTEMPTY` refusal cases of `AC-CLEANUP-BOUNDED`/`AC-CLEANUP-VALIDATE-FIRST`. If the contract ever requires direct cleanup of a live unpublished candidate or crash residue, the production capability yielding a valid `AcquiredCandidate` must be defined first — it is never satisfied by a test-only object. `writeEventFile` is the reentrant fallback only for a caller with no wider mutating transaction, and `applyChangeBundle` is the intentional exclusion, unreachable for an unpublished candidate. This criterion covers the candidate-lock cooperation boundary for the whole population; the fold-recovery behavior of the fold/`discardAndFoldEpoch` writers is B2's, not asserted here.
